questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence many have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.**

We look forward to an (1)/successful working relationship (2)/in the future. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'1' i.e. error lies in the first part of the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In part 1 of the sentence,** the usage of **'an' **is incorrect Instead, use** 'a'**

 
• The article ‘an’ is used before words that begin with vowels. In the given sentence, 'successful' starts with the consonant sound hence we need to use 'a' before this word.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• He is a good man. (good starts with the consonant sound hence the usage of article a is correct.)
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *We look forward to **a successful **working relationship in the future.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Teachers' Day shall be observed (1)/as non-teaching day (2)/in our campus. (3)/No Error (4)​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '2' i.e. error lies in part 2 of the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In part 2 of the sentence, the usage of **'non-teaching day'** is incorrect Instead, use 'a non-teaching day' 

 
• The article ‘a’ is missing before the word ‘non-teaching.’ The article ‘a’ would denote that it is one day.
 
• The word 'non-teaching is an adjective and this adjective is used attributively the structure for this is 'a/an/the +adjective + noun' so that's why we need to use an indefinite article before the adjective.

**So the correct sentence is-** *Teachers' day shall be observed as **a non-teaching day** in our campus.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Obligation​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Commitment". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Obligation" (**दायित्व ) refers to a duty or a commitment that compels someone to follow a particular course of action.
 
• It often involves a legal or moral requirement to do something or to refrain from doing something.
 
 
• Example: People have an obligation to follow the law to maintain order in society.
 
 
 
• The correct word **"Commitment" (**प्रतिबद्धता ) similarly means a pledge or a promise to do something and indicates a state of being bound emotionally or intellectually to a course of action.
 
 
• ​Example: He has a strong commitment to environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Denial: This means the action of declaring something to be untrue. (इनकार)
 
 
• Example: He shook his head in denial when asked if he had taken the money.
 
 
 
• Refusal: This refers to the act of saying no to a request, proposal, or demand. (अस्वीकृति)
 
 
• Example: Her refusal to cooperate made it difficult to complete the project on time.
 
 
 
• Declination: This signifies a polite refusal or a decrease in something. (पतन)
 
 
• Example: There was a noticeable declination in his academic performance due to his health issues.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

67, 64, 59, 52, ?
questions.solution:
The series follows the odd number subtraction rule starting from 3.

67 - 3 = 64

64 - 5 = 59

59 - 7 = 52

52 - 9 = 43

The next odd number after 7 is 9. Thus, subtracting 9 from 52, we obtain 43.

Therefore, 43 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 7 and their product is 12. What is the sum of their reciprocals?
questions.solution:
Let, two numbers are x and y

Sum of these two numbers is 7

x + y = 7 -----(1)

The product of these two numbers is 12

xy = 12 -----(2)

Divide equation (1) by xy

x/xy + y/xy = 7/xy

1/y + 1/x = 7/12

∴ Sum of their reciprocals is 7/12

questions.question: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 200 which are not multiples of 4?
questions.solution:
Multiples of 5 from 1 to 200 can be represented as 5n, where n is any natural numbers and 1 ≤ n ≤ 40

∴ Number of Multiples of 5 from 1 to 200 = 40

5n will be a multiple of 4 if n is a multiple of 4

Now, multiples of 4 from 1 to 40 can be represented as 4m, where m is any natural number and 1 ≤ m ≤ 10

∴ Number of multiples of 4 from 1 to 40 = 10

∴ Required number = 40 - 10 = 30

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by 9?
questions.solution:
A number will be divisible by 9 if the sum of the digits of the number is divisible by 9

Sum of digits of 234561 = 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 1 = 21, Not Divisible by 9

∴ 234561 is not divisible by 9

Sum of digits of 444123 = 4 + 4 + 4 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 18, Divisible by 9

∴ 444123 is divisible by 9

Sum of digits of 555231 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 21, Not Divisible by 9

∴ 555231 is not divisible by 9

Sum of digits of 65422 = 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 19, Not Divisible by 9

∴ 65422 is not divisible by 9

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days and A alone can do it in 30 days. B alone can do the work in how many days?
questions.solution:
A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days

Part of work A and B can do in 1 day = 1/20

A alone can do the work in 30 days

Part of work A can do in 1 day = 1/30

∴ Part of work B alone can do in a day = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60

∴ B alone can do the work in 60 days

questions.question: If 2/5th of a cistern is filled in 6 minute, then what is the time needed to fill the remaining part?
questions.solution:
Given,

Part of cistern filled in 6 minutes = 2/5

Part of cistern filled in 1 minute = 2/30 = 1/15

∴ Total time required to fill the cistern = 15 minutes

Remaining part to be filled = 1 - 2/5 = 3/5

∴ Required time to fill the remaining part = 15 - 6 = 9 minutes

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio of 6 : 5. If the perimeter of the field is 132 metres, then what is its breadth?
questions.solution:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2 (Length + Breadth)

Let,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67a4ce433b1dcaf544d56182853535a125849f4aa81007334a0a1398b0ceb2aa.png] 

The length and breadth are 6x and 5x respectively

∴ Perimeter = 2 (6x + 5x)

Given,

Perimeter = 132 m

∴ 2(6x + 5x) = 132

⇒ 11x = 66

⇒ x = 6

∴ Breadth = 5 × 6 m = 30 m

questions.question: A trader allows two successive discounts of 30% and 40% on selling an article. If he sells that article for Rs. 840, then what is the marked price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Let, marked price = Rs. x

After two successive discounts of 30% and 40%

Selling price

= x × {1 - (30/100)}{1 - (40/100)}

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 1050. A shopkeeper gives a discount of 30% and still makes a profit of 40%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the article?

**Detailed solution∶**

Marked price = Rs. 1050

Discount = 30%

∴ Selling price

= 1050 × (1 - 0.30)

= 1050 × 0.70 = 735

Given,

Profit percentage = 40%

We know,

Profit percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

40 = [(735 - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100

⇒ 0.40 × Cost Price = 735 - Cost Price

⇒ 1.40 × Cost Price = 735

⇒ Cost Price = 525

questions.question: A sum was invested on simple interest at a certain rate for 5 years. If the interest rate is increased by 2%, then the interest increases by Rs. 190. What is the sum (in Rs) invested?
questions.solution:
Simple interest = (P × r × t)/100

P = Principal

t = Time period

r = Rate of interest

Given,

t = 5 years

Let,

Principal = P

Rate of interest = r

Simple interest = (P × r × 5)/100 = Pr/20

After, increasing interest rate by 2% keeping amount of Principal and time fixed

Simple interest = [P × (r + 2) × 5]/100 = P(r + 2)/20

According to the question,

(Pr + 2P - Pr)/20 = 190

⇒ 2P = 20 × 190

⇒ P = 1900

questions.question: Which schedule of the Indian constitution deals with languages recognized by constitution?

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The Constitutional provisions relating to the Eighth Schedule occur in article 344(1) and 351 of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 344(1)** provides for the constitution of a Commission by the President on expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement, which shall consist of a Chairman and such other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule to make recommendations to the President for the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes of the Union.
 
• **Article 351** of the Constitution provides that it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India and to secure its enrichment by assimilating without interfering with its genius, the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and in the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule, and by drawing, wherever necessary or desirable, for its vocabulary, primarily, on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.

questions.question: The general name of the elements of **"Group 17"** is ______.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• A periodic table is an arrangement of elements based on their atomic numbers and chemical properties.
 
• It is divided into 18 groups and 7 periods running vertically and horizontally respectively.
 
• The periodic table accommodates a discrete combination of metal, non-metals, and metalloids.
 
• The elements in the periodic table are arranged horizontally in ascending order of their atomic numbers known as periods.
 
• Vertically the elements having identical chemical properties are clubbed together known as groups.
 
• The 18 groups are also known as columns and the 7 periods are also known as the rows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d16a8368d409900ed90309e3e688edcd632301cf42a7b2027cd2c23c0712d711.png] 

Explanation:__

Periods:

__
 
• Elements are arranged in increasing atomic number of the elements in a period.
 
• One extra electron gets added to the outermost shell as we move along the periods from left to right.
 
• The electron gets added to the same shell or orbit and thus the electrons present for bonding increase by one unit.
 
• Thus, the shell number remains the same but the number of electrons present for bonding increases along a period.

Groups:

 
• Elements having the same number of outer electrons are put in the same group of the periodic table.
 
• When we move down a group, one extra shell gets added to the elements.
 
• The outermost shell has electrons present for bonding.
 
• Though the number of shells increases as we go down in a group, yet the number of electrons in the outermost shell remains the same.
 
• For example, the Halogens F, Cl, Br, I, At all belong to group 17 and have 7 electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• Similarly, Group 16 elements have 6 electrons in the outermost shell, group 15 has 5 electrons in the outermost shell, and so on.
